details: Random counterexamples are a restriction of the adversarial equivalence-query model.
proof: An equivalence-query strategy that succeeds against every permissible counterexample also succeeds when the counterexample is selected randomly.  Thus $\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{req}}(\mathcal H)\le\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{eq}}(\mathcal H)=\mathrm{L}(\mathcal H)$.
name: Littlestone Dimension / Random Equivalence Queries Complexity
